subject: PoC economics & latency options — quant tiering + batch vs streaming follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie.park@fathomai.com>, Francis Moran <francis.moran@fathomai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: PoC economics & latency options — quant tiering + batch vs streaming follow-up

Thanks again for the call earlier, Ellie and Francis — good discussion. Quick recap and options for the PoC economics we promised: 

1) Volumes (your estimate): 12M prompts/month, average prompt length ~45 tokens, expected generation 120 tokens on average => ~2.0B tokens/month. You mentioned peak bursts up to ~3x baseline during monthly reporting windows.

2) Budget target: you flagged a mid-range target of $1.2k–$2.5k per 1M tokens for the initial PoC (flexible if we hit SLA guarantees). We sketched a target unit-econ of ~$1.8/1M tokens as a starting negotiation point.

3) Latency / tier trade-offs: options below — note we can route by policy so production can use lower-latency variants selectively.

   - Tier A (SLO 100–200ms): Dedicated low-latency instances, minimal batching, streaming responses. Higher unit cost (~x2 baseline). Good for interactive search and summarization UI.
   - Tier B (SLO 300–600ms): Aggressive CPU/GPU batching + KV prefix caching. Lower unit cost (~baseline). Best for background analysis and non-interactive bulk jobs.
   - Hybrid: Route interactive traffic to Tier A and batch analytics to Tier B. Use prefix caching for repeated user prompts to reduce tokens.

4) Quantization / model variants: 8-bit quant + smaller seq-length model for low-cost bulk processing; for high-quality interactive responses we recommend an fp16 variant with streaming. Expect 15–30% cost delta across variants.

Attached: PoC_estimate_v3.xlsx (worked numbers) and a short playbook on latency vs cost.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm which percent of traffic we should consider interactive vs batch (ballpark split e.g., 20/80, 50/50).
- We run a 2-week PoC with a dedicated pool for the interactive slice and put the remainder on a cost-optimized routing policy.
- I’ll send a refined PoC estimate by EOD tomorrow after you confirm split and any peak-day multiplier.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0114

From: Ellie Park <ellie.park@fathomai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Francis Moran <francis.moran@fathomai.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC economics & latency options — quant tiering + batch vs streaming follow-up

Thanks Jordan — useful recap. A couple clarifications: 

- The 12M prompts/month was conservative; internal analytics suggests closer to 18–20M prompts if we enable a short summary step in the ingestion pipeline. So tokens could be ~3.0–3.3B/month.
- For the interactive slice, our product PM is pushing for <250ms 95th for chat-like flows; about 40% of sessions are expected to be interactive in our early rollout (we can iterate).
- Budget is flexible but we’d like to keep effective spend under $5k/month for the first two months of PoC while we validate metrics.

Can you share the PoC_estimate_v3 with the assumptions line-by-line (token bands, model variant, estimated unit $/1M)? Also would like an explicit example of how routing policies would escalate from Tier B -> Tier A during peaks.

— Ellie
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie.park@fathomai.com>, Francis Moran <francis.moran@fathomai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC economics & latency options — quant tiering + batch vs streaming follow-up

Ellie — thanks, that helps. I attached an updated PoC_estimate_v3.xlsx with two scenarios (18M and 20M prompts). High-level line items below so you have them inline.

Scenario assumptions (20M prompts => ~3.3B tokens):
- Model variant assumptions:
  • Interactive (Tier A): fp16 7B-ish variant with streaming enabled; per-1M token baseline unit = $2.80 (we can discuss discounting based on commit).
  • Bulk (Tier B): 8-bit quant 7B variant optimized for batching; per-1M token baseline unit = $1.05.
- Effective split example (40% interactive / 60% bulk):
  • Interactive tokens: ~1.32B => cost @ $2.80/1M = $3,696
  • Bulk tokens: ~1.98B => cost @ $1.05/1M = $2,079
  • Estimated monthly spend = $5,775 (~$1.75/1M blended).

Options to hit $5k target for first two months: 
- Apply a 10% PoC discount on Tier A unit -> interactive unit becomes $2.52/1M (~-$130 on the interactive slice) AND enable aggressive prefix-caching on repeated prompts (~15% token reduction on bulk). That moves the blended spend to ~ $4.9k in the early months.
- If you need stronger guarantees on latency (95th <250ms) we recommend reserving a small dedicated pool (e.g., 2 low-latency replicas). The reservation adds a fixed monthly seat cost (~$1,100) but reduces cold-start and reduces variance during peaks. We can model that as an optional line item in the spreadsheet.

Routing policies / escalation (example):
- Normal: Interactive -> Tier A pool (reserved/low-latency), Bulk -> Tier B (cost-optimized autoscaling).
- Peak detection: If Tier B queue latency > configured threshold (e.g., 300ms p95) or if total tokens/min > X, automatically spill a % of traffic to Tier A up to a cap. Policy ensures we never exceed your budget cap (you set a hard spend cap). If we hit the cap we fall back to degraded model variant or return short-form results.

Action items:
- Jordan: update spreadsheet with the optional reservation line and the 10% PoC discount applied — I’ll share a final sheet by EOD.
- Ellie: confirm the interactive/bulk split (40/60 is fine to start) and whether we should model a reservation seat in month 1.
- Marissa: flagged for pricing review if we move from PoC discount to contractual pricing.

— Jordan
From: Francis Moran <francis.moran@fathomai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ellie Park <ellie.park@fathomai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC economics & latency options — quant tiering + batch vs streaming follow-up

Appreciate the split and the options, Jordan. Quick confirmation from our side:

- We’ll go with the 40/60 split for the PoC. Please model the reservation seat as optional (we’ll likely enable it if the reservation delta is less than $1.3k/month).
- Agreed to the 10% PoC discount on Tier A for the first 60 days.
- Please also show a worst-case peak scenario (3x tokens/minute spike) and a routing example where 30% of peak traffic spills to Tier A. We want to understand both budget impact and latency guarantees in that case.

If you can get the updated spreadsheet and a short one-page routing diagram in the Drive folder today, we’ll lock timing for a PoC kickoff early next week.

Thanks — Francis
